subject: Seller-led buyer journey & term-length discussion for AWS Marketplace listing
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalysthealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Catalyst Health Procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: AWS listing — buyer approvals & term length question

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of our procurement folks asked for clarification before we move forward with a private offer via AWS Marketplace:

- What contract term lengths do you typically support when customers purchase via a private offer (1/2/3 years vs annual auto-renew)?
- How does buyer approval gating work on your side — do you require an SOW or PSA for co-sell deals, or can we sign a single PO against the Marketplace private offer?

I've attached our procurement checklist for reference. Can we get a short note we can share internally (legal/procurement)?

Appreciate it,
Laura

Attachments: catalyst_procurement_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS listing — buyer approvals & term length question

Hi Laura — thanks for sending this over and for the good discussion yesterday. Summary for procurement/legal to circulate internally:

1) Term lengths we support via AWS private offers
- Standard: 12 months (annual) — most common and fastest to close.
- Multi-year: 24 or 36 months supported; requires explicit seller approval and pricing lock documentation.
- Auto-renew: We can support auto-renew on annual terms but prefer explicit renewal for multi-year commitments to ensure capacity planning.

2) Procurement & approvals
- Buyer can submit a single PO against the private offer SKU. That PO is valid for the purchase term you select.
- For co-sell/PSA work (professional services, onboarding), we either: 
  a) Attach an SOW/PSA to the contract outside of the Marketplace billing (common), or
  b) Include a statement of work as a separate DocuSign linked to the PO (if procurement requires a single point of record).

3) Security/compliance notes
- We can provide SOC2 artifact links and a runbook for data residency on request.

Next steps: if you confirm preferred term length and whether you'd like PS/Onboarding on the PO vs separate SOW, we will prepare the private offer and a short one-page summary for your legal/procurement.

Best,
Mina
Director, Partnerships (Redwood Inference)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalysthealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS listing — buyer approvals & term length question

Laura — quick note from pricing/marketplace ops:

- Pricing: for multi-year deals we typically apply a stepped discount schedule. Example: 12mo = standard list, 24mo = ~8% off list, 36mo = ~12% off list (subject to volume). We can provide a formal tier once you share expected ARR/usage.
- Approval gating: buyer's procurement approval is sufficient at purchase time. On our side, multi-year offers need internal commercial approval (CD approval + marketplace entry). That approval timeline is usually 24-72 hours once we have the PO and expected ARR.

I can prepare a one-pager with these bullets and a sample private offer timeline if that helps procurement.

-Vanessa
Senior Marketplace Ops (Redwood Inference)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalysthealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS listing — buyer approvals & term length question

Adding notes from co-sell/PSA perspective:

- If Catalyst wants Redwood to be seller-led on the listing (we own the private offer, billing, and baseline support), then the SOW for any professional services should live externally (DocuSign) but reference the PO for invoicing alignment.
- If you prefer joint billing (Catalyst purchases product via Marketplace, then contracts PS with a reseller), that's workable but we'll need a brief reseller agreement route and co-sell enablement (I can loop AWS GTM).

Suggested approach for speed:
1) Opt for a 12-month private offer to get started quickly.
2) Sign a short SOW for onboarding PSA outside Marketplace (DocuSign link).
3) At month 9 we run a renewal/expansion review — if you want a multi-year lock we can convert then with a pricing adjustment.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call with procurement/legal to walk through the one-pager.

--Vivek
Head of Field Partnerships (Redwood Inference)
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@catalysthealth.com>

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement prefers the PO to be the single source of record, but they will accept an external SOW if it references the PO and invoicing cadence.

Action items for us:
- We will proceed with a 12-month private offer to expedite procurement sign-off.
- Procurement asked for a sample private-offer summary (term, billing cadence, renewal policy) and a draft PO template from Redwood.

I've attached our procurement checklist again and flagged the PO template field. Can you share the sample summary + PO template by EOD Monday (2026-11-08)?

Thanks,
Laura

- Term: 12 months, billing monthly in arrears (can convert to annual invoicing on request).
